title: Donald Trump signs lucrative deal with criminal-supported Bayrock Group
description_short: Donald Trump signs lucrative deal with criminal-supported Bayrock Group
description_medium: NPR reported that Trump’s Trump SoHo deal licensed his name to the developers and included management fees and an 18% equity share, according to his deposition. Bayrock’s former finance director later alleged that the firm handled illicit funds; Bayrock denied money-laundering allegations. The reporting does not establish that Trump knew of or joined any alleged wrongdoing.
description_long: The Trump SoHo project in lower Manhattan involved Trump, Bayrock Group and the Sapir Organization. NPR reported that the deal licensed Trump’s name for the condominium hotel and paid him management fees; in a deposition, Trump said he also held an 18% equity share. The project was under construction by 2006. Bayrock’s former finance director, Jody Kriss, later alleged in a lawsuit that the company concealed illicit overseas money through real-estate transactions. Bayrock denied money-laundering allegations, and Kriss’s suit was in settlement talks when NPR reported on the dispute. One Bayrock principal, Felix Sater, had served prison time for assault and pleaded guilty in a securities-fraud case, according to NPR. Trump said he knew little about Sater and said he had not known of his financial crimes; other depositions and later statements described more contact between them. These details document a licensing relationship and disputed allegations about Bayrock’s financing, but they do not establish that the company itself was criminally convicted or that Trump knew of or participated in money laundering. The article distinguishes the business arrangement from claims made in litigation.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump signs lucrative deal with criminal-supported Bayrock Group
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump signs lucrative deal with criminal-supported Bayrock Group

notes: NPR’s report supports the name-licensing arrangement, Trump’s stated 18% equity share and a former finance director’s money-laundering allegations, which Bayrock denied. The report does not establish that Trump knew of or participated in those allegations. Proposed correction: change “criminal-supported Bayrock Group” to a neutral description of the Trump SoHo licensing deal and preserve allegations as attributed claims.

title: Trump: Russia fakes an ISIS terrorist attack in Louisiana on anniversary of 9/11
description_short: Trump: Russia fakes an ISIS terrorist attack in Louisiana on anniversary of 9/11
description_medium: A supplied timeline describes a Russian Internet Research Agency hoax on September 11, 2014, claiming that ISIS had bombed a chemical plant in Centerville, Louisiana. It says the false story appeared through cloned U.S. news sites, social-media posts and emergency text alerts to some residents. The account does not link the operation to Donald Trump.
description_long: The supplied timeline describes a fabricated report circulated on September 11, 2014, that ISIS had attacked a chemical plant in Centerville, Louisiana. It attributes the operation to Russia’s Internet Research Agency and says the false claim was amplified through social-media posts, copies of U.S. news websites and emergency alert texts reportedly sent to some Louisiana residents. The timeline also refers to doctored videos, but its excerpt does not describe what they showed or how widely they circulated. These methods were presented as an effort to make a nonexistent attack resemble breaking news from several sources at once. The material supplied here does not establish how many residents received alerts, what local authorities did in response, whether the hoax caused a public-safety disruption, or how the operation was independently attributed. Most importantly, it provides no evidence connecting the 2014 incident to Donald Trump. The episode can be described as a reported disinformation operation, but placing it under a Trump-prefixed title implies a relationship not documented in the source material.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Russia fakes an ISIS terrorist attack in Louisiana on anniversary of 9/11

notes: The linked timeline page returned only a short error response, and the supplied summary provides no direct Trump connection. It also does not establish the hoax’s reach or outcome.
